The majority of workers would be hired locally, with approximately 25 percent to be transferred to the area from Applicant's other projects. Approximately 80 percent of the transferees (20 percent of the entire work force) are expected to move their families with them. The Applicant estimates that construction of this project would result in 100 new families relocating in the area.
Employment in the local construction industry would increase as a result of the Bad Creek Project and new workers would contribute to the economy of the Oconee-Pickens County area in both wages spent and taxes paid. Assuming 95 percent of the 500-man work force either relocates or resides in the project vicinity, the annual wages paid would be on the order of $6 million in the local economy, minus social security contributions and Federal taxes (475 men x 40 hrs. x 52 wks. x $6/hr). This would represent roughly 1 percent of all labor and proprietors' earnings for 1972 in the two counties.
Project construction would also contribute to the local economy, including that of the Greenville-Spartanburg area, through the purchase of building materials available in local markets. This would encourage further employment gains in the local building supply and related industries, exclusive of any multiplier effects on the rest of the economy.
Approximately 500 acres within and surrounding the project would be cleared prior to construction. The removal of this land from timber production would have little if any effect on the local economy.
Construction of this project would have an effect on transportation in two ways. The planned relocation of 0.4 mile of Route 171 would disrupt traffic on that highway for the period of its relocation. In addition, the large numbers of workers commuting to the site during construction would greatly increase the amount of traffic on those few roads serving the project area.
